items.text:
You have to defend these men on principle, the principle of individual rights, or watch this exchange repeat until nothing is left to defend. Here is the newest round.

Ackman finds a real flaw. Under the plan, a founder whose company dies owes ordinary taxes on the forgiven debt, insolvency plus garnished wages for life. A devastating point, offered as a detail. And Khanna's answer? Bill, appreciate the push on the details. Then he drafts the patch on the spot: the founder pledges his shares for a government loan, and if he cannot repay, the state assumes the shares.

Read that twice. The objection improved the bill, and the improved bill ends with government owning equity in startups. The wealth tax matured into partial nationalization inside one reply, and the critic was thanked as a co-author.

This is what arguing mechanics earns. Every flaw you find, they fix. Every detail you push, they refine. The one thing they cannot survive is the argument most people with a platform refuse to make: the founder's wealth is his by right, earned by consent, and no need on earth converts it into public property. Concede that, and you are not the opposition. You are the drafting committee.


Ro Khanna (@RoKhanna)

Bill, appreciate the push on the details. 

Under a non-recourse structure, when the government takes the pledged shares there is no ordinary debt-forgiveness income and no personal liability. The transfer is treated as a sale of the shares for the amount of the loan. That produces capital gain or loss, not ordinary income, and the government cannot garnish wages or go after other assets for the loan itself.

You’re right that if the shares go to zero the founder can still face capital gains tax on the deemed sale (basis is often near zero). That’s a real issue. The regulations if the ballot passes should explicitly address that, either non-recognition treatment when the government assumes the shares under this program, or limiting the amount realized to actual fair market value. We can write that in cleanly. The ballot initiative already has a deferral mechanism for illiquidity.

The goal is straightforward. Give founders of illiquid private companies a workable way to meet a one-time wealth tax without a forced fire sale that hurts the company and the jobs. Most of the 250 California billionaires hold public stock and don’t face this problem. For the minority who do, a deferral mechanism or a properly drafted non-recourse option with clear tax treatment is a practical bridge, not a trap. 

We only need this money because the Trump administration cut $30 billion to our Medicaid program.  If folks hadn't supported Trump and his medicaid cuts, maybe we wouldn’t need this.



— https://nitter.net/RoKhanna/status/2089149245735506147#m

items.text:
This so-called defense of the founders by Cuban is worse than Ro Khanna's direct assault, because it is the assault's enabler, as their exchange below illustrates.

Watch the sequence. Mark's first reply argued only mechanics. The founders are cash poor, the banks will not lend, capital will flee. Not one sentence said the wealth is not the state's to take. So Ro did what a man of consistent premises always does when handed the premise: he solved the mechanics. Sell the shares, or the state will sell them for you. That sentence was not a gaffe, Mark. It was your own argument, completed. You told him the problem was collection, and he collected.

And read your rage carefully, because its shape confesses the same surrender. Every line of it defends the founders' effort, their jobs created, their wages paid, their reinvestment. Which means the fortune must be earned twice, once by building it and again by social service, before you will object to its seizure. And your own contrast gives away the rest: Jensen and Lisa Su have liquidity, so taxing them raises no cry. Then your objection is not the taking. It was to the timing. A man who concedes that much has no answer when the state offers to fix the timing, and none when a politician measures the seizure against poor kids, since need as a claim on ability is the one premise nobody in this thread has challenged.

Here is the answer that ends the argument. The wealth is theirs. Not because they are illiquid, not because they create jobs, not because they suffered for it, but because they earned it in voluntary trade, and no need anywhere on earth converts another man's property into public revenue. Say that, and there is nothing left to negotiate. Refuse to say it, and your profanity is just the sound a pragmatist makes when his own premise comes back to collect.


Mark Cuban (@mcuban)

Ro, “in your scenario, the founder could sell to pay a one time 5 percent tax or the state could sell it if he defaults on the loan” 

Ro, this is the biggest fuck you in the history of entrepreneurship.  Ever.  

Creating jobs but don’t have cash.  Fuck you 

Can’t sell shares, we will sell it for you, to whoever.   Fuck you.  

Creating jobs. Paying great wages instead of taking cash out yourself.   Fuck you

Reinvesting into your company and community.  Fuck You. 

Don’t you know that Jensen, and Lisa Su, and people who have vast amounts of liquidity already have no problem with it.  Fuck You 

There is a huge difference between someone  with liquidity , running a huge public company, and someone who has dedicated every minute of who knows how many years,  to building a company, to finally have a dream financing come true , only to be insulted by a politician.  “We will sell your shares for you “

GTFO

🚨🚨 BREAKING NEWS: Blasphemy law is back — but it only applies to Muslims.

FSU member and retired police officer Stephen Gray was found guilty of being "grossly offensive", a criminal offence under s127 of the Communications Act 2003, for repeating a joke about Mohammed. 

Stephen reposted a message he saw on Facebook that said: “Fun facts about bacon! People who eat bacon have a lower chance of marrying a 9 year old!”

While giving evidence, Stephen explained that the post was a reference to the marriage between the Prophet Mohammed and Aisha — which was consummated when she was just nine years old, after he married her when she was six.

Stephen said the post was intended to be satirical but he also hoped it would spark a serious debate: did that marriage, as recorded in the Hadiths, contribute to the acceptability of child marriage in Muslim countries?

District Judge Steven Hood found the post to be “grossly offensive” and dismissed Stephen's defence that it was making a serious political point about the acceptability of child marriage. He found that the post was designed to be offensive and could not be making a serious point because it was light-hearted in nature. He concluded that a conviction would not amount to a disproportionate interference with Stephen’s right to freedom of expression.

The Free Speech Union is helping Stephen appeal his conviction and has instructed a top criminal silk, John Beggs KC, to act for him.

With your support, we hope to be able to pay for Stephen’s legal defence in the Crown Court and meet the costs of any further appeals. Please donate Stephen's crowdfunder in the link below.

Earlier this year, the FSU paid for the defence of Hamit Coskun, who burnt a copy of the Quran outside the Turkish consulate in London. He was initially convicted, but we managed to get that conviction overturned on appeal. When the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) then tried to appeal the acquittal, we took them on and won again.

More recently, the Free Speech Union threatened South Wales Police with legal action after it adopted a draconian version of the Government’s definition of anti-Muslim hostility, instructing officers to record any comment that went beyond “legitimate” discussion of Islam as a 'non-crime hate incident'. We won, and the force withdrew the guidance.

Stephen’s case gives us another opportunity to reaffirm the principle that there is nothing illegal about criticising any religion, including Islam.

It should not be a criminal offence to repost jokes about Islam that some Muslims find offensive.

Read more below and please donate to our Crowdfunder 👇
